quote: a mapping from states to probabilities of selecting each possible action
reason: "a mapping from states to probabilities of selecting each possible action", the object that learning changes [@sutton2018].

quote: use RL to optimize a language model policy to produce responses assigned high reward without drifting excessively far from the original model
reason: The language model itself is the policy: RLHF methods "use RL to optimize a language model policy to produce responses assigned high reward without drifting excessively far from the original model" [@rafailov2023]; PPO and DPO both move it from the pretrained prior [@ouyang2022].
note: Supports model-as-policy and a drift limit from the original model. The named KL form and PPO are not in this quote.

quote: GRPO foregoes the critic model, instead estimating the baseline from group scores, significantly reducing training resources
reason: The model is the policy, and "GRPO foregoes the critic model, instead estimating the baseline from group scores, significantly reducing training resources" [@shao2024]; the same method is used for reasoning training in [@deepseekai2025].
note: Supports the critic-free group-relative part. The claim that the trace is part of the output is not in this quote, so the reason drops it.

quote: To make parsing individual steps easier, we train the generator to produce solutions in a newline delimited step-by-step format
reason: The policy is the generator model with a step boundary: "To make parsing individual steps easier, we train the generator to produce solutions in a newline delimited step-by-step format" [@lightman2024]; at inference a process verifier scores each step [@snell2024].
note: Supports model plus step delimiter. PRM-as-value-for-search is from snell2024, not quoted.

quote: it is becoming more popular to take advantage of LLMs as a policy model for decision making, especially in interactive environments
reason: In an agent the model acts as the policy: "it is becoming more popular to take advantage of LLMs as a policy model for decision making, especially in interactive environments" [@yao2023b]; RL on such a model updates weights [@wei2025].
note: Supports LLM-as-policy in interactive settings only. Nothing quoted says the scaffold parses tool calls, is fixed code, or that RL leaves it unchanged. Reason weakened.

note: The cell reason cites no work, so no quote may be taken.

quote: For all tasks, GPT-3 is applied without any gradient updates or fine-tuning, with tasks and few-shot demonstrations specified purely via text interaction with the model
reason: The weights stay frozen and adaptation is in context: "For all tasks, GPT-3 is applied without any gradient updates or fine-tuning, with tasks and few-shot demonstrations specified purely via text interaction with the model" [@brown2020].
note: Directly supports frozen weights with adaptation through text.

quote: a frozen large language model, PaLM-540B (Chowdhery et al., 2022)1 , is prompted with few-shot in-context examples to generate both domain-specific actions and free-form language thoughts for task solving
reason: The agent policy is a frozen model steered from outside the weights: "a frozen large language model, PaLM-540B (Chowdhery et al., 2022)1 , is prompted with few-shot in-context examples to generate both domain-specific actions and free-form language thoughts for task solving" [@yao2023b]; tool use is added in [@schick2023].
note: Supports frozen model changed by prompt. Scaffold and tool set are not in the quote; schick2023 is cited for tools.

quote: For EHRAgent, it originally initializes its knowledge base with only four experiences and updates its memory dynamically
reason: An agent can carry memory it updates over time: "For EHRAgent, it originally initializes its knowledge base with only four experiences and updates its memory dynamically" [@chen2024]; the wider setting is discussed in [@hammond2025].
note: Supports a memory store that the agent updates. Sub-agents and policy inputs being its own earlier outputs are not supported by the quote. Reason weakened.
